questions.prompt: How many pairs of legs does an adult insect have?

Two
Four
Eight

Two: head and abdomen

questions.prompt: What material primarily forms the exoskeleton of insects?

Cellulose
Calcium carbonate
Keratin

options: Through a network of tracheae that opens to the outside through spiracles
Through lungs connected to the mouth
Through gills beneath the abdomen
By absorbing oxygen only through the legs

questions.imageCaption: Honey bee, example illustrating this question about insects.

questions.prompt: What are the main purposes of an insect’s antennae?
options: To detect sensory signals, including odors
To perceive ambient light
To propel the insect in flight
To pump the blood

questions.imageCaption: Honey bee, example illustrating this question about insects.

questions.prompt: How do gerrids, like water skaters, move across the surface of a pond?

They swim below the surface by propelling their fringed hind legs
They cling to emerged plants to move out of the water
They propel themselves by expelling a jet of water from the abdomen

questions.prompt: Why does an insect have to molt to grow?
options: Its rigid cuticle does not continually grow with it
Its bony shell cannot stretch
He must renew his blood to grow
Its wings must grow back each season

questions.didYouKnow: Insects are part of arthropods, like spiders and crustaceans.
questions.imageCaption: Honey bee, example illustrating this question about insects.

questions.prompt: What are the respiratory openings visible on the bodies of many insects called?
options: Spiracles
Tracheae
Air sacs
Gills

questions.imageCaption: Honey bee, example illustrating this question about insects.

A closed circulation where the blood remains in a network of vessels
A dual circulation separating oxygenated and non-oxygenated blood
An open circulation whose fluid is propelled by several peripheral cores

Holding the wings in place during flight
Direct the air towards the spiracles
Attach the insect to the plant while it feeds

Membranous hindwings used to steer
Gills beneath the wing covers
Jointed plates that cover the legs

questions.prompt: What do many adult and larval ladybugs feed on?

Nectar and pollen
Leaves and seeds
Of wood and bark

To seize prey
To filter particles in water
To pierce leaves to lay eggs

A sound produced by the elytra
A silk trail
An odorous secretion

Scaly forewings
An abdominal stinger
Long jumping legs

Forewings in half elytra
Delightful paws
Antennae ending in a fan

questions.prompt: Which sense is enhanced by the fan-like antennal plates of many scarab beetles?

The vision
The hearing
The taste

By lungs

Specialized flower herbivores
Internal fish parasites
Aquatic filter feeders

It remains inside the egg until fully developed

Floral nectar
Small aquatic animals
Animal debris

They degrade rocks

It is bred as a predator of mosquitoes

Swimming hind legs

Of feathers

To place the eggs in the wood

Conifer needles
Flower nectar
Decaying wood

It molts directly into a smaller adult
